passage: Rain drummed on the tin roof in a small town in Mizoram. Lalremsiami had read her last message to Zoram so many times that she knew it by heart: "Maybe I talked too much about my exams." He had not replied for nineteen days. On Saturday at the tea stall she told Shalini everything. "You have said that line to me three times," Shalini said gently. "Did you insult him? No. It is just a loop." Lalremsiami laughed weakly. That night she wrote in her notebook: "I said nothing wrong. He did not answer. I am allowed to close this myself." She put the phone in the drawer and slept.

qa.q: How many days had Zoram not replied?
qa.a: He had not replied for nineteen days.

qa.q: How was Lalremsiami feeling as she kept rereading her last message?
qa.a: She was anxious and blaming herself, rereading it until she knew it by heart as if she had said something wrong.

qa.q: What steps helped Lalremsiami get out of the loop?
qa.a: She talked to Shalini, heard the loop named, wrote down that she said nothing wrong and put the phone away.

qa.q: How does Shalini see Lalremsiami's repeated line?
qa.a: Shalini sees it as a loop, not proof of a mistake, and answers gently by asking if there was any insult.

grounding: After being ghosted the person replays what she said, notices the loop, talks to a friend and gives herself closure.

passage:
After Pankaj stopped replying in October, I did something I'm not proud of: I replayed our last conversation about two hundred times. Was it the joke about his job? The way I said "see you soon" too eagerly? I scrolled up so often I knew his messages by heart.
One night my friend Shirin found me doing it at 1 a.m. in the hostel common room. She sat down and said, "You've told me this story five times this week. Has it changed?"
It hadn't. That was the loop. Hearing it named helped.
She said, "Write him the goodbye he didn't give you. Don't send it." So I did, in my notebook: what I enjoyed, what hurt, and that I was done waiting. It took twenty minutes. At the end I felt tired but lighter.
I still think of him sometimes. But now when the replay starts, I notice it, and I text Shirin instead of scrolling.
— Ujjwal

qa.q: How many times did Ujjwal replay the last conversation?
What was Ujjwal feeling while replaying the conversation?
qa.a: Hurt and anxious, blaming the joke about the job and the too-eager "see you soon".

qa.q: What helped Ujjwal step out of the loop?
qa.a: Shirin naming the loop, writing an unsent goodbye in a notebook, and texting Shirin instead of scrolling when the replay starts.

qa.q: How does Shirin see Ujjwal's retelling?
qa.a: As a loop that never changes; she gently names it and suggests a way out.

grounding: Shows replaying what went wrong after being ghosted, noticing the loop, talking to a friend and giving oneself closure.

passage:
Counsellor's note, student wellness centre, 7 December
Irawati came in today, her third visit. Her close friend Hafsa stopped replying two months ago, after a disagreement over a group trip. Irawati said she has been lying awake "rewriting every message" and has decided the friendship ended because she is "too much".
I asked her to list, on paper, the evidence for "too much". She found one argument and two late replies. Then I asked what she would tell a friend in her place. She laughed a little: "That they're not the only one in the story."
We talked about noticing the loop: when she catches herself rereading the chat, she will write the thought down, then text her cousin or go for a walk. She also plans to write herself a closing note to Hafsa that she will not send.
Her shoulders looked less tight when she left. We meet again next week.

qa.q: How long ago did Hafsa stop replying?
What had Irawati decided about why the friendship ended, and how was it affecting her?
qa.a: That it ended because she is "too much"; the self-blame kept her lying awake, anxious and rewriting messages.

qa.q: What plan did Irawati make with the counsellor?
qa.a: Notice the loop, write the thought down and then text her cousin or walk, and write an unsent closing note to Hafsa.

qa.q: What does Irawati's answer about "not the only one in the story" suggest about Hafsa's part?
qa.a: That Hafsa also played a part, so the silence isn't only Irawati's fault.

grounding: Illustrates rumination and self-blame after being ghosted by a friend, and noticing the loop and giving oneself closure with support.
